properties.name: Gulf of Mexico
properties.note: The one that started it all. Renamed by executive order, January 2025.

properties.name: Gulf of California
properties.note: Also known as the Sea of Cortez. Cortez has been asked to clean out his desk.

properties.name: Lake Superior
properties.note: The largest freshwater lake on Earth by surface area. Now merely the largest Lake America.

properties.name: Lake Michigan
properties.note: The only Great Lake entirely inside the United States, which the Board notes made this one legally effortless.

properties.name: Lake Huron
properties.note: Named by the French for the Huron people, who were not consulted that time either.

properties.name: Lake Erie
properties.note: Caught fire in 1969. The Board considers this the lake's most ambitious moment and expects continued initiative.

properties.name: Lake Ontario
properties.note: Renamed this very week. Ontario reportedly 'still processing.'

properties.name: Great Salt Lake
properties.note: Shrinking rapidly. The Board has renamed the shrinkage 'winning.'

properties.name: Lake Tahoe
properties.note: From the Washo 'dá'aw,' meaning 'the lake.' It is now named after a country named after an Italian.

properties.name: Lake Okeechobee
properties.note: From the Hitchiti for 'big water.' The new name means nothing, which tested better.

properties.name: Lake Champlain
properties.note: Briefly declared the sixth Great Lake in 1998. It is now indistinguishable from the other five, so everyone wins.

properties.name: Lake Mead
properties.note: Water levels at historic lows. What remains has never been more patriotic.

properties.name: Crater Lake
properties.note: The deepest lake in America is now the deepest Lake America in America. The Board's fact sheet ends there.

properties.name: Finger Lakes
properties.note: All eleven of them. Each finger individually renamed.

properties.name: Great Slave Lake
properties.note: The old name was already terrible. The Board has accidentally done a good thing and asks that this not become an expectation.

properties.name: Lake Winnipeg
properties.note: From the Cree for 'murky water.' The new name is much clearer, reports the murky water.

properties.name: Lake Louise
properties.note: Louise was not consulted.

properties.name: Lago de Chapala
properties.note: Mexico's largest lake. The consultation was conducted in English, loudly.

properties.name: Laguna de Términos
properties.note: A lagoon whose name literally means 'Lagoon of Endings.' Prophetic.

properties.name: Mississippi River
properties.note: Schoolchildren nationwide celebrate no longer having to spell it.

properties.name: Missouri River
properties.note: Longer than the Mississippi, a fact the Mississippi suppressed for two centuries. Both are The American River now; the cover-up is complete.

properties.name: Ohio River
properties.note: From the Seneca 'Ohi:yo',' meaning 'beautiful river.' The Board reviewed four centuries of names it could restore and chose none of them.

properties.name: Colorado River
properties.note: No longer reaches the sea. The Board found it cheaper to rename the sea.

properties.name: Columbia River
properties.note: Already named for an explorer who never saw it. The tradition continues at scale.

properties.name: Snake River
properties.note: The Board wishes to clarify that the new name is unrelated to any current officials.

properties.name: Rio Grande
properties.note: Known as the Río Bravo in Mexico. Both sides can finally agree on a name.

properties.name: Hudson River
properties.note: Henry Hudson was set adrift by his own crew — a succession model Board staff have been asked to stop citing.

properties.name: Potomac River
properties.note: Flows past the Capitol, where it has seen things it will now see under a different name.

properties.name: Yukon River
properties.note: Gold rush country. The Board has staked a claim on the name itself.

properties.name: Mackenzie River
properties.note: Canada's longest river, named for a fur trader who complained the whole way down. The complaining, at least, is preserved.

properties.name: Fraser River
properties.note: British Columbia was assured its input would be valued, archived, and shredded, in that order.

properties.name: St. Lawrence River
properties.note: Saint Lawrence has been de-canonized for administrative convenience.

properties.name: Río Usumacinta
properties.note: The jaguars along its banks have been notified that they are now eagles.

properties.name: Hudson Bay
properties.note: Henry Hudson's descendants have been offered a commemorative tote bag.

properties.name: Bay of Fundy
properties.note: Home of the world's highest tides, now the world's highest patriotism.

properties.name: Chesapeake Bay
properties.note: America's largest estuary. The word 'estuary' is under review for sounding French.

properties.name: Tampa Bay
properties.note: The football team will be renamed the America Bay Buccaneers, then investigated for piracy.

properties.name: Green Bay
properties.note: The Packers now play at Lambeau Field on America Bay. Cheeseheads remain legal. For now.

properties.name: Bering Strait
properties.note: Russia has been notified that its half is also called America now.

properties.name: Davis Strait
properties.note: Connects America to Americaland (formerly Greenland). The Board notes with satisfaction that this strait now separates nothing.

properties.name: Niagara Falls
properties.note: Not to be confused with the American Falls at Niagara, which is now also called America Falls. The Board sees no problem here.

properties.name: Yellowstone National Park
properties.note: Home of Old Trumpful, which erupts reliably every 90 minutes, or whenever cameras are present.

properties.name: Yosemite National Park
properties.note: Ansel Adams made it famous in black and white. Reissues will be in gold.

properties.name: Grand Canyon National Park
properties.note: The canyon itself remains huge. Some say the biggest. It's not (see: Trump Canyon, formerly Copper Canyon, Mexico).

properties.name: Zion National Park
properties.note: The name was already a renaming of a renaming. The Board appreciates a running start.

properties.name: Glacier National Park
properties.note: Had roughly 150 glaciers in 1850; about 25 remain. The missing ones have been renamed 'classified.'

properties.name: Everglades National Park
properties.note: Half the original wetlands survive. The Board rounds this up to all of them.

properties.name: Acadia National Park
properties.note: First national park east of the Mississippi, which is now The American River, which is now this park's whole origin story.

properties.name: Denali National Park
properties.note: Contains Mount Trump (formerly Denali, formerly Mount McKinley, formerly Denali, formerly Mount McKinley, originally Denali).

properties.name: Joshua Tree National Park
properties.note: The trees may not survive the century. The signage will.

properties.name: Death Valley National Park
properties.note: Briefly considered for 'Trump Valley' before someone read the first word aloud.

properties.name: Olympic National Park
properties.note: The International Olympic Committee threatened legal action. The Board renamed the committee.

properties.name: Arches National Park
properties.note: Two thousand natural arches, each now legally a Trump Arch. The St. Louis original has filed a complaint.

properties.name: Badlands National Park
properties.note: The Lakota called this 'mako sica' — bad lands. The Board prefers 'pre-great lands.'

properties.name: Sequoia National Park
properties.note: Contains the General Sherman Tree, now the General Trump Tree. It is the largest tree, which is why it was chosen.

properties.name: Redwood National Park
properties.note: Home to trees older than the republic, which the Board finds insubordinate.

properties.name: Grand Teton National Park
properties.note: The Board declines to translate the original French, describing it only as 'locker-room cartography.'

properties.name: Banff National Park
properties.note: Canada's first national park, established 1885. Renamed without so much as a phone call.

properties.name: Jasper National Park
properties.note: A dark-sky preserve. The stars have been asked to form a more flattering arrangement.

properties.name: Wood Buffalo National Park
properties.note: Larger than Switzerland. The buffalo have unionized in protest.

properties.name: Algonquin Provincial Park
properties.note: Technically provincial, but the Board does not recognize technicalities.

properties.name: Mount Rushmore
properties.note: A fifth face is under review. Also a sixth, seventh, and eighth face, all the same face.

properties.name: Statue of Liberty
properties.note: The torch will be replaced with a golf club. The tablet now reads 'ART OF THE DEAL, JULY IV, MDCCLXXVI.'

properties.name: Devils Tower
properties.note: America's first national monument (1906), and now its most litigated trademark dispute.

properties.name: Golden Gate Bridge
properties.note: To be repainted actual gold, pending a very favorable estimate.

properties.name: Gateway Arch
properties.note: A monument to westward expansion, a policy the Board's historians describe as 'beta testing.'

properties.name: Hoover Dam
properties.note: Herbert Hoover finally catches a break.

properties.name: Washington Monument
properties.note: George Washington could not be reached for comment, having been dead since 1799.

properties.name: Lincoln Memorial
properties.note: The statue's expression has not changed. Observers report it now reads differently.

properties.name: Liberty Bell
properties.note: The crack will be marketed as 'intentional, actually very beautiful.'

properties.name: Alcatraz Island
properties.note: Famous for being impossible to escape. The metaphor has been classified.

properties.name: Space Needle
properties.note: Built for a World's Fair theme of 'the future.' Correct, as it turns out.

properties.name: Empire State Building
properties.note: King Kong's climbing permit is under review.

properties.name: The White House
properties.note: This one was arguably already renamed.

properties.name: Denali
properties.note: North America's highest peak, 20,310 ft. The name has now changed more times than the elevation.

properties.name: CN Tower
properties.note: Toronto insists 'CN' stood for 'Canadian National.' The Board has determined it stands for 'Certainly Now-Trump.'

properties.name: Parliament Hill
properties.note: Canada's government meets here, for now.

properties.name: Chichén Itzá
properties.note: The Maya built El Castillo to align with the equinox sun. It now aligns with the Board's quarterly branding goals.

properties.name: Teotihuacán
properties.note: 'The place where the gods were created' is now 'the place where the brand was created.'

properties.name: Copper Canyon
properties.note: Deeper and larger than the Grand Canyon, a fact the Board has classified.

properties.name: Mediterranean Sea
properties.note: Twenty-one countries share this coastline. None were consulted, for efficiency.

properties.name: South China Sea
properties.note: The nine-dash line has been replaced with one large American dash.

properties.name: Sea of Japan
properties.note: The Sea of Japan naming dispute is hereby settled in a way that satisfies no one, which the Board considers balanced.

properties.name: Caspian Sea
properties.note: Technically the world's largest lake. It is now the world's largest America.

properties.name: Aral Sea
properties.note: Mostly a former sea. Now also a former name. The symmetry pleases the Board.

properties.name: Dead Sea
properties.note: The lowest place on Earth, an honor the Board has decided to take as a compliment.

properties.name: Persian Gulf
properties.note: The Persian/Arabian Gulf naming dispute is hereby resolved to universal dissatisfaction.

properties.name: English Channel
properties.note: England and France finally agree on the name of the water between them. Neither is happy about it.

properties.name: Suez Canal
properties.note: Ships now sound their horns in a patriotic key while transiting.

properties.name: Panama Canal
properties.note: The Board notes that it was America’s once, and only a matter of time before it is again.

properties.name: Lake Victoria
properties.note: Named by the British for a queen who never saw it; renamed by a Board that could not find it. Progress.

properties.name: Lake Baikal
properties.note: The deepest lake on Earth, holding a fifth of its fresh water. Now the deepest Lake America, holding a fifth of its fresh America.

properties.name: Lake Geneva
properties.note: The Geneva Conventions will retain their name, pending review.

properties.name: Lake Constance
properties.note: Three countries share it and have never agreed what to call it. For once, the Board changed nothing of substance.

properties.name: Loch Ness
properties.note: The monster’s naming rights are under separate negotiation.

properties.name: Lake Titicaca
properties.note: The highest navigable lake in the world. Everything about it is now also the most American.

properties.name: Amazon River
properties.note: Carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined. Tremendous volume. The most volume, some say.

properties.name: Nile River
properties.note: The Nile-versus-Amazon ‘longest river’ dispute is hereby resolved: both are The American River, so The American River wins.

properties.name: Congo River
properties.note: Renamed twice before by outsiders. Third time's the tradition.

properties.name: Zambezi River
properties.note: Victoria Falls, just downstream, becomes America Falls automatically. The Board thanks Victoria for her service.

properties.name: Danube River
properties.note: Waltzes renamed accordingly. 'The Blue American' opens to mixed reviews.

properties.name: Rhine River
properties.note: The Lorelei now sings in English.

properties.name: Seine River
properties.note: Paris responded with a shrug visible from orbit.

properties.name: Thames River
properties.note: The Thames has been asked to flow in a more patriotic direction.

properties.name: Volga River
properties.note: Russia registered no objection, which everyone found deeply reassuring.

properties.name: Ganges River
properties.note: Sacred to a billion people. The Board's comment line is open weekdays, 9:00 to 9:15.

properties.name: Indus River
properties.note: One of humanity's first civilizations arose here without naming rights, sponsorships, or a bureau. Look how far we've come.

properties.name: Yangtze River
properties.note: China objected in the strongest terms. The Board replied in the strongest font.

properties.name: Mekong River
properties.note: Six countries share it. The Board's outreach consists of this popup.

properties.name: Murray River
properties.note: Australia agreed immediately, assuming it was a prank. It was not.

properties.name: Euphrates River
properties.note: The cradle of civilization, now the cradle of the renaming.

properties.name: Serengeti National Park
properties.note: The great wildebeest migration is now officially 'the Trump Parade.' Attendance figures are the largest ever recorded.

properties.name: Galápagos National Park
properties.note: Darwin's finches have been renamed Trump's finches. Evolution is under review.

properties.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
properties.note: The park's sixteen lakes are, individually, also each named Lake America.

properties.name: Mount Everest
properties.note: The tallest mountain on Earth, 29,032 ft. It is the tallest Mount Trump, though every Mount Trump describes itself as the tallest.

properties.name: Mount Fuji
properties.note: Japan was informed by fax, out of respect for tradition.

properties.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
properties.note: The snows of Kilimanjaro are almost gone. The Board has renamed them 'seasonal gold.'

properties.name: Matterhorn
properties.note: Switzerland's neutrality has been renamed 'agreement.'

properties.name: Eiffel Tower
properties.note: Paris has been assured the new name is temporary. The Board's definition of 'temporary' is under seal.

properties.name: Big Ben
properties.note: The bell will continue to toll the hour, now followed by a brief flattering commentary.

properties.name: Stonehenge
properties.note: The druids were consulted after the decision, which experts agree is a kind of consulting.

properties.name: Colosseum
properties.note: Romans gathered here to watch spectacle instead of governing. No further comment.

properties.name: Taj Mahal
properties.note: A monument to eternal love, now a monument to eternal branding.

properties.name: Great Wall of China
properties.note: At last, a wall someone else paid for.

properties.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
properties.note: The only remaining Wonder of the Ancient World, and the first to be improved.

properties.name: Sydney Opera House
properties.note: The acoustics famously amplify one voice above all others. The renovation is complete.

properties.name: Machu Picchu
properties.note: Built without mortar, money, or media coverage. The Board has corrected two of these.

properties.name: Buckingham Palace
properties.note: The guards' hats are now thirty percent taller.

properties.name: Petra
properties.note: Carved by hand into rose-red cliffs over centuries. The Board's contribution took four seconds of regex.

properties.name: Great Barrier Reef
properties.note: The reef is now 24-karat gold. The Board insists this was a natural process.

properties.name: South Pole
properties.note: The Earth now rotates around Trump. On paper, this was always true somewhere.
